text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Following confessions of alcoholism, Swedish Left Party leader Gudrun Schyman, is to take time off from politics to deal with her problem.

- Swedes are increasingly optimistic that the economy is about to pick up, with 21 percent of households in August believing the economy will improve in the next 12 months, compared to 17 percent in July, according to Statistics Sweden.
- Volvo and Saab automobile producers continue to lose ground in the Swedish and foreign markets, having lost nine percent in sales so far this year in Sweden.
- Ferry traffic between Gotland, Sweden's largest island, and the mainland is to be taken over by ferry operator Gotlandsbolaget from 1998 in collaboration with the Finnish Silja Line.
- The Swedish government has partially backed down on its unpopular proposal to tighten tax on company cars after complaints that it would hurt the Swedish car industry.
- Swedish manufacturing industry gathered momentum over the summer, with the purchasing managers' index reaching 54.3 percent in August compared to 48.4 percent in July.

- Sweden's clothing retailers staged a recovery this year, following a major slump in 1995. Swedish Hennes & Mauritz had 6.2 percent of the Swedish retail clothing market during the first half of 1996, up from 5.7 percent during the same period last year.
- Swedish bonds are among the most successful government papers, with Italian bonds coming second, and Spanish bonds third, according to global worldwide index Effas.
